In summary, our research is concerned with
a new problem, namely, how to transmit extra bits over a coded payload link with negligible performance degradation.
the problem of reliable transmission of extra bits on top of the coded transmission link, without any cost of additional energy or bandwidth.
the transmission of additional information over a coded payload link, without the cost of extra transmission power or bandwidth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the extra bits are reliably transmitted with negligible performance loss to the payload link, and the extra bits can be transmitted at a rate up to 60 bits per second for the LDPC-coded transmission of a 2.4 Gb/s payload.
the proposed superposition transmission of the extra bits can be reliable and has a very small effect on the performance (in terms of the bit error rate) of the coded payload links.

the superposition transmission is feasible, and can be implemented with low-complexity codes and low-complexity decoding algorithms, and that it can achieve a rate close to the channel capacity for the case of LDPC coded transmission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for LDPC coded transmission, the accessible capacity is about half of the channel capacity, and it can be achieved by transmitting extra bits with random superposition.

, by exploiting the accessible capacity of LDPC-coded transmission, a free ride on the existing coded payload link is feasible, and the extra bits can be used for a variety of applications such as data authentication and channel coding for the payload link.

, with a very low rate LDPC payload code, we can achieve a high rate of extra bits transmission without sacrificing the performance of the payload link, and this is possible by exploiting the gap to the channel coding limit of the LDPC payload code.
The main takeaway from our work is that

extra bits can be transmitted over the existing coded transmission link with negligible effect on the original coded link, which can potentially lead to a new design philosophy for future wireless systems.
the accessible capacity of the payload link can be used as an extra resource for data transmission, which is not exploited by the existing coded transmission scheme.
, by exploiting the gap to the channel capacities of practical codes, it is possible to transmit extra bits without any additional cost of energy or bandwidth.
